title: Sanjeev Kapoor's Pineapple Sheera: A Step-by-Step Guide to the Festive Dessert
excerpt: The celebrity chef's fruity take on the classic semolina dessert combines roasted rawa, ghee and fresh pineapple — a simple, festive sweet that takes about an hour.
body:
• Celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor has shared a recipe for pineapple sheera, giving the classic semolina dessert a fruity twist ahead of the festive season.
  • The recipe combines roasted semolina, ghee and sugar with fresh pineapple, finished with cardamom, nutmeg, saffron, cashews and pistachios.
  • Properly roasting the semolina until golden and fragrant is the key step — it gives sheera its aroma and prevents a raw taste.
  • The dessert takes about an hour in total and is an easy, vegetarian option for festive meals and family gatherings.

With the festive season approaching, celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor has shared a recipe that gives a familiar Indian dessert a refreshing turn: pineapple sheera. The traditional semolina-based sweet gets the flavour of fresh pineapple, making it an option for festive meals, family gatherings or simply an indulgent dessert at home, according to Hindustan Times.

What Makes Sheera Work

Sheera — also called rava or sooji halwa — is one of the most comforting desserts in Indian cooking. At its simplest, it is fine semolina roasted in ghee, cooked with water or milk and sweetened with sugar. What elevates it is the technique: the semolina must be roasted patiently until it turns golden and releases its nutty aroma. Kapoor's version keeps that foundation and adds diced fresh pineapple, whose natural sweetness and tang cut through the richness of the ghee.

The Recipe: Step by Step

Ingredients: ½ medium pineapple, 1 cup fine semolina (barik rawa), ¾ cup ghee, 1 cup + 2 tablespoons sugar, ½ teaspoon green cardamom powder, ¼ teaspoon nutmeg powder, 1 tablespoon saffron water, roasted chopped cashews and blanched slivered pistachios for garnish.

  1. Peel the pineapple, remove the core and cut the flesh into small dices.
  2. Heat 3 cups of water in a deep non-stick pan. Add the green cardamom powder, nutmeg powder and saffron water, mix, and bring to a boil.
  3. Heat the ghee in a non-stick kadai. Add the semolina and sauté on medium heat, stirring continuously, until light golden brown. This step is important: properly roasted semolina gives sheera its characteristic aroma and prevents the finished dessert from tasting raw. Take care that it doesn't stick to the pan or brown too much.
  4. Add the diced pineapple to the roasted semolina and continue to sauté until the semolina turns a deeper golden brown, letting the fruit combine with the ghee-coated grain.
  5. Carefully add the boiled spiced water to the mixture, mix well, cover and cook on low heat for 5 to 6 minutes.
  6. Add the sugar, mix well and cook on medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until the sugar dissolves completely. Take the pan off the heat and let the sheera rest for 15 to 20 minutes.
  7. Transfer into a serving bowl, sprinkle the roasted cashews and pistachios on top, and serve.

Tips for Getting It Right

Prep time is 30 to 35 minutes with another 30 to 35 minutes of cooking, and the recipe is rated easy on Kapoor's site. A few things matter: use barik (fine) rawa rather than coarse semolina for a smooth texture, roast the semolina patiently over low to medium heat rather than rushing it, and let the sheera rest before serving so the grains finish absorbing the moisture. Tinned pineapple can stand in for fresh in a pinch — Kapoor's site also carries a version using tinned pineapple with milk.

Serving and Variations

Pineapple sheera is best served warm, garnished generously with nuts. It pairs well with a festive thali or as a standalone dessert. For a more indulgent take, Kapoor has also demonstrated a version stuffed with vanilla ice cream — warm sheera around a cold centre, served immediately.
